title: Disposition Request
description:
A developer's REQUEST that a specific finding be dispositioned. Distinct from the disposition itself.

WHY THIS EXISTS: enforcement without a request path leaves humans communicating with the pipeline by interpretive dance. A team that cannot ask for a review will disable the workflow instead, which is strictly worse than an advisory mode.

TWO LIFECYCLES, DELIBERATELY NOT ONE ENUM:
  request_state     REQUESTED -> UNDER_REVIEW -> APPROVED | REJECTED | CHANGES_REQUESTED
                    ... the GOVERNANCE workflow: where this request has got to.
  requested_disposition  FALSE_POSITIVE | ACCEPTED_RISK | MITIGATED | REMEDIATED
                    ... the SECURITY determination: what is claimed to be true.

Collapsing them produces a dashboard cheerfully reporting that a vulnerability is 'APPROVED', which says nothing whatsoever about what was approved.

AUTHORITY: a request is not a disposition. Only a MERGED approval on the protected default branch alters enforcement. A PR cannot approve its own request -- otherwise a developer adds FALSE_POSITIVE beside the secret they just introduced and the same PR passes.

finding_ref.description: Points at the IMMUTABLE original observation. The request never edits it.

requested_disposition.description: THE SECURITY CLAIM. What the requester says is true about the finding.

request_state.description: THE GOVERNANCE STATE. Where the request has got to. Never conflated with the claim above.

requester.description: Who is asking. MUST NOT equal review.reviewer -- implementer is not reviewer.

justification.description: Why the requested classification holds. 'Please ignore the scanner' is not a justification.

evidence_refs.description: Links to the evidence supporting the CLAIM. What counts differs by type -- see conditional requirements.

review.description: Filled by the security-approver ROLE. Reviewing is establishing whether the proposed classification is actually supported -- not clicking Approve.

reviewer.description: The ROLE that reviewed, never a person's name. A pipeline routed to an individual becomes an undocumented API, and needs reconstructive surgery when they leave.

ticket_ref.description: External work item (an external work-item system). Designed in NOW so the same contract can later be driven by their workflow without changing the security model.

governance.description: What the disposition would carry if approved. Reviewed, not merely proposed.

external_ref.description: Optional upstream identifier so a request can originate outside GitHub without redesigning the contract.

allOf.$comment: MITIGATED means a compensating control exists. Naming it is what separates mitigation from acceptance.
ACCEPTED_RISK means the finding is REAL and someone chose to proceed. That choice needs a record and an end date.
REMEDIATED asserts the condition is GONE. It must be verifiable by re-scanning, and is the only claim the scanner itself can falsify.
Approval requires a reviewer and a rationale. An approval with neither is a rubber stamp with extra steps.
